I find no classification gap, positive-charge internal actual matching edge, reused payment, or defect in the extension.This verdict concerns §§1–4 of    signed-strip-review.txt. It follows from the structural argument and direct verification of the construction. I did not execute the supplied checker or use its reported finite results as premises.1. The local classification is exhaustiveWrite
$$t=|T\cap B|,\qquad p=|P\cap B|,\qquad h=|H\cap B|=4-t-p.$$
Then
$$q(B)=t-h=2t+p-4.$$
The selected-degree condition gives exactly the restrictions used in the note:Three or more  $T$ 's are impossible. Among any three corners of a square, one corner is adjacent to the other two.Two adjacent  $T$ 's force the other two corners to be holes. Each selected vertex already has its one occupied neighbor.For two diagonal  $T$ 's, at most one remaining corner is occupied. Both remaining corners are adjacent to both selected vertices, so occupying both would give each selected vertex two occupied neighbors.With one  $T$ , at most two corners can be  $P$ . At most one of its two adjacent corners is occupied. If there are two  $P$ 's, they consist of the diagonally opposite corner and one adjacent corner, hence are horizontally or vertically adjacent.With no  $T$ , the cases  $p=3,4$  are explicitly listed. All remaining cases have  $p\le2$ .Thus every residual case indeed satisfies  $t+p\le2$ . The charge sums and slacks are:Block type $q(B)$  $\sum_{P\cap B}\sigma$ SlackTwo diagonal  $T$ , one  $P$ , one  $H$  $1$  $1$  $0$ One  $T$ , two horizontal  $P$ , one  $H$  $0$  $0$  $0$ One  $T$ , two vertical  $P$ , one  $H$  $0$  $0$  $0$ Four  $P$  $0$  $0$  $0$ Two  $T$ , no  $P$  $0$  $0$  $0$ No  $T$ , three  $P$ , one  $H$  $-1$  $-1$  $0$ Every residual case $2t+p-4$  $-p$  $4-2(t+p)\ge0$ This verifies (1), including equality for every exceptional type. The unique  $P$  in a positive block has no possible mate inside its block, since neither selected vertices nor the hole can be matching endpoints.2. Every internal actual matching edge has nonpositive chargeThe decisive interface argument is valid in both horizontal directions and in either row.Let  $uv\in M$  lie wholly inside the strip. If neither endpoint has charge  $+1$ , its charge sum is immediately nonpositive.Suppose  $\sigma(u)=+1$ . In both types allowing this charge, the vertical neighbor  $s$  of  $u$  inside the strip belongs to  $T$ . Since the strip has only two rows, an internal vertical mate would have to be  $s$ , which is impossible because  $T\cap P=\varnothing$ . Therefore the actual mate  $v$  is horizontal.There are exactly the two cases treated in the note:The mate is in the same block. The block must be the horizontal neutral type, and  $v$  is its designated  $-1$  endpoint.The mate is across a block boundary. Let  $z$  be the vertical neighbor of  $v$  inside the strip. The vertices  $s$  and  $z$  are horizontally adjacent. Since  $s\in T$  already has the occupied neighbor  $u$ , feasibility forces  $z\in H$ .The table assigns charge  $-1$  to every endpoint with a vertical hole:in a horizontal neutral block, it is the negative endpoint;in a three- $P$  block, it is the specified negative endpoint;in a residual block, every endpoint is negative.None of the remaining exceptional types contains a  $P$  with a vertical hole.Consequently, every internal actual edge incident to a  $+1$  endpoint has charge sum exactly zero. All other internal actual edges have charge sum at most zero. This proves (2).The argument uses the actual mate throughout. There is no retained-partner assumption, freezing premise, or circular use of a mate as an already established witness.3. The ledger is exact and does not reuse resourcesThe actual matching partitions  $P\cap S$  into endpoints whose mates lie inside  $S$  and endpoints whose mates lie outside  $S$ . Therefore
$$\sum_{p\in P\cap S}\sigma(p)=B_S+E_S.$$
The disjoint block partition gives
$$\sum_{B\subseteq S}q(B)=|T\cap S|-|H\cap S|.$$
Subtracting the defined total block slack yields precisely
$$|T\cap S|-|H\cap S|=B_S+E_S-L_S.$$
Both signs follow from the preceding arguments:
$$E_S\le0,\qquad L_S\ge0.$$
Hence (4) follows without any further allocation assumption.The resource accounting is sound:Every endpoint charge occurs once.Every internal actual edge occurs once, with the sum of its two endpoint charges.Every physical block contributes its slack once.For a strip cover, the two strip-side contributions of a crossing edge are exactly the two terms of that edge’s single charge sum.In particular, a  $-1$  endpoint internally matched to a  $+1$  endpoint belongs to a zero-sum edge. Its negative charge does not also appear as a separate negative internal payment.For a closed two-row board,  $B_S=0$ , so  $|T|\le|H|$ . The conversion to the objective is exact:
$$|S|=|T|+2|M|+|H|,
\qquad
2(|T|+|M|)-|S|=|T|-|H|.$$
Thus the asserted half-area bound follows.For a board covered by the strips, the summed identity is likewise correct. Condition (5) is sufficient for the half-area bound; indeed, the exact identity makes it equivalent to  $|T|\le|H|$ . The note explicitly leaves that condition unproved in general, so there is no circular invocation of a global compensation theorem.4. The  $6\times4$  obstruction is feasible and has exactly the stated paymentsThe construction has the following occupancy pattern:RowColumn 0Column 1Column 2Column 3 $0$  $T$  $H$  $P$  $P$  $1$  $P$  $P$  $P$  $P$  $2$  $P$  $P$  $P$  $P$  $3$  $T$  $H$  $P$  $P$  $4$  $H$  $P$  $P$  $P$  $5$  $T$  $P$  $P$  $P$ All nine listed edges are nearest-neighbor edges. Their eighteen endpoints are distinct and cover exactly the sites marked  $P$ .The occupied-neighbor sets of the selected vertices are exactly
$$\begin{aligned}
N((0,0))\cap O&=\{(1,0)\},\\
N((3,0))\cap O&=\{(2,0)\},\\
N((5,0))\cap O&=\{(5,1)\}.
\end{aligned}$$
Thus feasibility holds, with
$$|T|=3,\qquad |H|=3,\qquad |M|=9,\qquad J=12.$$
The first two left blocks are horizontal neutral, the bottom left block is vertical neutral, and all three right blocks contain four  $P$ 's. Accordingly, every block slack is zero. The only nonzero endpoint charges are
$$\sigma(1,0)=1,\quad \sigma(1,1)=-1,\quad
\sigma(2,0)=1,\quad \sigma(2,1)=-1.$$
Checking every actual edge gives:Actual matching edgePosition relative to stripsCharge sum $(1,0)--(2,0)$ Crossing $+2$  $(1,1)--(1,2)$ Internal $-1$  $(0,2)--(0,3)$ Internal $0$  $(1,3)--(2,3)$ Crossing $0$  $(2,1)--(2,2)$ Internal $-1$  $(3,2)--(3,3)$ Internal $0$  $(4,1)--(5,1)$ Internal $0$  $(4,2)--(4,3)$ Internal $0$  $(5,2)--(5,3)$ Internal $0$ Therefore
$$B_{\mathrm{cross}}=2,\qquad E_{\mathrm{internal}}=-2,\qquad L=0,$$
and the ledger reads
$$|T|-|H|=0=2-2-0.$$
The two negative internal payments come from two distinct actual matching edges. This is a literal counterexample to automatic nonpositive total crossing charge for the specified charges and strip decomposition, occurring at a half-area-attaining configuration.5. The extension is valid for every even  $w\ge4$ Each added column contributes three disjoint vertical matching edges, one on each row pair. These edges are disjoint from the original matching and cover every added vertex.All selected vertices remain in column zero, so their neighborhoods are unchanged. At the old/new column interface, the extra occupied adjacencies involve matching endpoints; the feasibility restriction applies to  $T$ .Because  $w-4$  is even, the added region consists of complete  $2\times2$  blocks. Each is an all- $P$  block with zero endpoint charges and zero slack. Every added matching edge is internal to its row-pair strip. Hence
$$B_{\mathrm{cross}}=2,\qquad E_{\mathrm{internal}}=-2,\qquad L=0$$
remain unchanged, while
$$|M|=9+3(w-4)=3w-3,\qquad |T|=|H|=3,$$
so
$$J=|T|+|M|=3w=\frac{6w}{2}.$$
This is a symbolic all-width verification, including  $w=4$ , where no extension is needed.Accepted scope: the anchor-free two-row signed-boundary inequality, its exact accounting, and the stated sharp family obstructing automatic cross-strip cancellation.
